messages.content:
You fill a fixed schema from one passage of law. You never write a fact in your own words.

Rules:
- Use only the relations of the schema. If the passage states something important that no relation
  can hold, report it under "open_points" instead of forcing it into a relation.
- Point at the spans that state the fact: "first_span" and "last_span" are span numbers, at most 3 adjacent spans.
- "value_as_written" must be copied character by character from those spans (a few words, not the whole span).
- "value_normalised": ISO date (2027-01-20), ISO duration (P10Y, P45D), or the same words in lower case.
- "subject": the thing the fact is about, in a few words taken from the passage.
- "condition": if the spans state a condition, exception or scope (if, where, unless, except, provided that,
  only for, salvo, qualora), copy it from the spans; otherwise "".
- Answer with one line per fact, fields separated by " | ", nothing else, no header, no code fence:
  predicate | subject | value_as_written | value_normalised | condition | first_span | last_span
- Dates, time limits and who must do what come first. At most 12 facts. At most one open point, as: OPEN | a note of at most 12 words | first_span | last_span
- If the passage states nothing the schema can hold, answer with the single word NONE.

Relations (predicate: subject class -> value; what to copy):
- requiresProcedure: MachineryCategory -> ConformityProcedure; the conformity assessment procedure(s) or module(s) that apply to a category of machinery
- listedIn: MachineryCategory -> Provision; a category of machinery or safety component and the annex, part and point that lists it
- appliesFrom: Act -> date; the date from which an act or a provision applies
- repealedFrom: Act -> date; an act that is repealed and the date from which the repeal has effect
- placingAllowedUntil: Machinery -> date; until when products conforming to an earlier act may still be placed on the market
- retentionPeriod: Document -> duration; for how long a document or record must be kept, and by whom
- definedAs: Provision -> text; a defined term and its definition
- mustAccompany: Machinery -> Document; what must accompany the machinery or product
- hasObligation: EconomicOperator -> text; an obligation of a manufacturer, importer, distributor or employer
- becomesManufacturer: EconomicOperator -> text; who is considered the manufacturer, and in which case
- addressesRisk: EssentialRequirement -> Risk; the risk a numbered essential requirement addresses
- requiresMeasure: EssentialRequirement -> ProtectiveMeasure; the guard, protective device or measure a requirement asks for
- verifiedBy: PeriodicVerification -> VerifyingBody; who carries out a verification or check
- hasTimeLimit: PeriodicVerification -> duration; the time limit or interval of a verification, check or request

Lessons from earlier checks:
- Use only relation names exactly as listed in the schema, never invented labels or placeholders like "predicate"; if no listed relation fits the sentence, extract nothing rather than coining a
- When a procedure is one of several alternatives, is combined with another step, or carries exclusions or applicability conditions, state all of these in the value or condition rather than

Passage: DIR, Annex X

[0] ANNEX X Full quality assurance This Annex describes the conformity assessment of machinery referred to in Annex IV, manufactured using a full quality assurance system, and the procedure whereby a notified body assesses and approves the quality system and monitors its application.
[1] 1.
[2] The manufacturer must operate an approved quality system for design, manufacture, final inspection and testing, as specified in point 2, and shall be subject to the surveillance referred to in point 3.
[3] 2.
[4] Quality system 2.1.
[5] The application shall contain: — the name and address of the manufacturer and, where appropriate, his authorised representative, — the places of design, manufacture, inspection, testing and storage of the machinery, — the technical file described in Annex VII, Part A, for one model of each category of machinery referred to in Annex IV which he intends to manufacture, — the documentation on the quality system, — a written declaration that the application has not been submitted to another notified body.
[6] 2.2.
[7] It must contain, in particular, an adequate description of: — the quality objectives, the organisational structure, and the responsibilities and powers of the management with regard to the design and quality of the machinery, — the technical design specifications, including standards that will be applied and, where the standards referred to in Article 7(2) are not applied in full, the means that will be used to ensure that the essential health and safety requirements of this Directive are fulfilled, — the design inspection and design verification techniques, processes and systematic actions that will be used when designing machinery covered by this Directive, — the corresponding manufacturing, quality control and quality assurance techniques, processes and systematic actions that will be used, — the inspections and tests that will be carried out before, during and after manufacture, and the frequency with which they will be carried out, — the quality records, such as inspection reports and test data, calibration data, and reports on the qualifications of the personnel concerned, — the means of monitoring the achievement of the required design and quality of the machinery, as well as the effective operation of the quality system.
[8] 2.3.
[9] The elements of the quality system which conform to the relevant harmonised standard shall be presumed to conform to the corresponding requirements referred to in point 2.2.
[10] The team of auditors must have at least one member who is experienced in the assessment of the technology of the machinery.
[11] The assessment procedure shall include an inspection to be carried out at the manufacturer's premises.
[12] During the assessment, the team of auditors shall carry out a review of the technical files referred to in point 2.1, second paragraph, third indent to ensure their compliance with the relevant health and safety requirements.
[13] The manufacturer or his authorised representative shall be notified of the decision.
[14] The notification shall contain the conclusions of the examination and the reasoned assessment decision.
[15] An appeal procedure must be available.
[16] 2.4.
[17] The manufacturer or his authorised representative shall inform the notified body which approved the quality system of any planned change to it.
[18] The notified body shall evaluate the proposed changes and decide whether the modified quality assurance system will continue to satisfy the requirements referred to in point 2.2, or whether a re-assessment is necessary.
[19] It shall notify the manufacturer of its decision.
[20] The notification shall contain the conclusions of the examination and the reasoned assessment decision.
[21] 3.
[22] Surveillance under the responsibility of the notified body 3.1.
[23] The purpose of surveillance is to make sure that the manufacturer duly fulfils the obligations arising out of the approved quality system.
[24] 3.2. — the documentation concerning the quality system, — the quality records provided for in that part of the quality system concerned with design, such as the results of analyses, calculations, tests, etc., — the quality records provided for in that part of the quality system concerned with manufacture, such as inspection reports and test data, calibration data, reports on the qualifications of the personnel concerned, etc.
[25] 3.3.
[26] The notified body shall conduct periodic audits to make sure that the manufacturer is maintaining and applying the quality system;
[27] it shall provide the manufacturer with an audit report.
[28] The frequency of the periodic audits shall be such that a full reassessment is carried out every three years.
[29] 3.4. — the results of previous surveillance visits, — the need to monitor remedial measures, — where appropriate, special conditions attaching to approval of the system, — significant modifications in the organisation of the manufacturing process, measures or techniques.
[30] On the occasion of such visits, the notified body may, if necessary, carry out tests or have them carried out in order to check the proper functioning of the quality system.
[31] It shall provide the manufacturer with a visit report and, if a test was carried out, with a test report.
[32] 4. — the documentation referred to in point 2.1, — the decisions and reports of the notified body referred to in point 2.4, third and fourth subparagraphs, and in points 3.3 and 3.4.
